article_paragraphs: After taking a look at the two wheeler sales , let us now take a look at the car sales, which have reached 5,24,226 units in October 2026, up 12.18% from 4,67,289 units in October 2025. Maruti Suzuki accounted for nearly half of the 64,769 units added over September, while Tata Motors and Mahindra finished just 556 units apart in the race for second place.

Maruti Suzuki led with 2,12,384 units, up 20.46% YoY and 16.80% MoM. Its volumes increased by 36,066 units over October last year and by 30,546 units over September. With sales growing faster than the overall market in both comparisons, Maruti’s share rose to 40.51%, from 37.73% a year ago and 39.58% in September.

Tata Motors retained second place with 73,894 units, up 20.87% YoY and 7.39% MoM. Its market share increased to 14.10% from 13.08% a year earlier. However, Tata’s monthly volume growth lagged the overall market, pulling its share down from September’s 14.98%.

Mahindra sold 73,338 units, up 2.39% YoY and 14.43% MoM. It added 9,246 units over September, against Tata’s gain of 5,084 units. That narrowed Tata’s lead from 4,718 units in September to 556 in October. Mahindra’s market share edged up from 13.95% to 13.99% month on month, while remaining below the 15.33% it held in October 2025.

Hyundai placed fourth with 62,799 units, up 16.74% YoY and 9.85% MoM. Its share rose to 11.98% from 11.51% a year ago, but fell from 12.44% in September. Kia followed with 33,462 units, up 13.22% YoY and 4.51% MoM. Kia’s share stood at 6.38%, compared with 6.32% a year earlier and 6.97% in September.

Toyota recorded 29,521 units, up 17.96% MoM but down 26.67% from the 40,257 units it sold a year ago. Its share improved from 5.45% in September to 5.63% in October, against 8.62% in October 2025. Toyota posted the largest year-on-year volume decline among the manufacturers listed, selling 10,736 fewer units.

JSW MG held seventh place with 8,013 units, up 25.26% YoY and just five units below September. Skoda followed at 7,805 units, down 5.42% YoY but up 27.91% MoM. Honda was just 196 units behind Skoda at 7,609 units. Honda’s sales grew 19.00% YoY and 70.41% MoM, lifting its market share from 0.97% in September to 1.45% in October.
Renault rounded out the top 10 with 4,577 units, down 2.03% YoY but up 34.66% MoM. Nissan sold 3,594 units, up 37.44% YoY and 8.91% MoM. Its share increased to 0.69% from 0.56% a year earlier.

An electric version of the more premium Urbania is also under development and it will launch within a few months of the launch of Traveller EV. Adaption of electric mobility in larger commercial vehicles over Diesel fuel will be gradual over the years, when compared to smaller cars and SUVs.

However, there are a few applications like school buses, employee transportation and intracity ambulances where electric mobility plays a viable role. Tourism and small inter-city applications are probable applications for electric powertrains right now. Other than the e-Traveller Smart Citibus EV, more variants are likely to launch.

Force Motors has pledged an investment of Rs 3,000 Crores across engineering, electrification, hybrid driveline technology and digitisation. Also, the company has committed to manufacturing capacity expansion that will accommodate increased demand in the future with Traveller EV and Urbania EV.

title: TVS Ntorq 150 Spectral Green Launched At Rs. 1.22 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The new dark olive green shade is exclusive to the top-spec TFT variant and gets fluorescent yellow accents alongside black alloy wheels TVS Motor Company has introduced a new Spectral Green colour option for the Ntorq 150 in India priced at Rs. 1.22 lakh (ex-showroom, Delhi) and it follows the same treatment for Jupiter a while ago. It is exclusively available on the top-spec TFT variant at no additional cost. The update comes just over a year after the Ntorq 150 made its Indian debut. The Spectral Green colour uses a dark olive green base that contrasts against fluorescent yellow accents on the front mudguard and rear body panels. The side panels feature grey and yellow Ntorq 150 graphics while the alloy wheels receive a gloss black finish. The darker treatment distinguishes it from the brighter colour combinations offered previously. The TFT variant now has four colour options comprising Spectral Green, Nitro Green, Racing Red and Turbo Blue. The new colour option does not introduce any mechanical revisions as you might expect as the Ntorq 150 retains its 149.7 cc single-cylinder three-valve air-cooled engine. The motor develops 13.2 PS at 7,000 rpm and 14.2 Nm at 5,500 rpm. Power is transmitted to the rear wheel via a continuously variable transmission. TVS claims acceleration from zero to 60 kmph in 6.3 seconds and a maximum speed of 104 kmph. The scooter also gets Street and Race riding modes alongside the iGo Assist system. The Spectral Green version receives the existing 5-inch colour TFT instrument console and TVS SmartXonnect connectivity. The system supports turn-by-turn navigation, smartphone notifications, music controls, Alexa integration and smartwatch connectivity. Other functions comprise vehicle tracking, geo-fencing, crash alerts and over-the-air software updates. The TFT variant also gets traction control while single-channel ABS is also available. A four-way handlebar controller operates the digital display. The scooter uses an underbone chassis supported by telescopic front forks and a rear monoshock. The 12-inch alloy wheels are fitted at both ends while braking duties are handled by a 220 mm front disc and a 130 mm rear drum. Its kerb weight stands at 115 kg and the seat height measures 770 mm along with a ground clearance of 155 mm. On the outside, it boasts distinctive quad LED projector headlamp arrangement, angular front apron, aerodynamic winglets and exposed handlebar. The front combination lamps sit beneath the headlamp assembly while the rear gets a T-shaped LED tail lamp. The compact exhaust and sculpted side panels are other highlights. The Ntorq 150 also offers 22 litres of underseat storage and a fuel tank capacity of 5.8 litres. The Ntorq 150 is currently available in two variants. The regular version costs Rs. 1.13 lakh while the TFT version is priced at Rs. 1.22 lakh (all prices, ex-showroom, Delhi). The Ntorq 150 competes against sporty scooters such as the Yamaha Aerox 155, Aprilia SR 175 and Hero Xoom 160.

summary: … with a spotlight on the Great Wall Motor ORA 5 rising star. CleanTechnica readers were probably hoping for the surge to keep surging Down Under. However, it appears to have remained steady. Not the flash in the pan petrolheads were hoping for at least.
article_paragraphs: … with a spotlight on the Great Wall Motor ORA 5 rising star.

CleanTechnica readers were probably hoping for the surge to keep surging Down Under. I was. However, it appears to have remained steady. Not the flash in the pan petrolheads were hoping for at least. In September 2026, 108,778 passenger vehicles were sold, including all drivetrains. See the charts here .

Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) achieved a market share of 24.2% (26,287 units) , outselling petrol-only and diesel-only vehicles. Add in 10,072 plugin hybrid (PHEV) sales and you get a plugin penetration rate of approximately 34%. PHEV sales are the fastest growing segment in Australia — increasing 122% year on year. For those who care, 17,843 HEVs sold in October (a YoY increase of 20%). I am looking forward to peak HEV, followed by peak PHEV, as we have seen in more mature Scandinavian markets.

Australia’s EV penetration rate (including BEV and PHEV) has hovered in the low to mid 30% for the last few months. Not sure what the future holds, but even just maintaining this rate for a few months will make a difference. Nothing beats lived experience. My neighbours are now asking about how much it costs to fill up. One came for coffee yesterday and stayed to go for a drive in our new Model Y. He was very impressed with the tech, the finish, and above all the running costs. He confided that he had just filled up his wife’s Honda Civic — AU$82 — and his Isuzu D Max — AU$121.

On a recent shopping expedition, we counted 10 electric cars in the car park, out of 50 vehicles. Not just Tesla and BYD, but also Zeekr, Geely, the GWM ORA 5, and a Deepal. Battery electric vehicles are making their presence felt. But not all my friends can see them. They can spot Tesla and BYD vehicles, but they tell me they don’t see any other EVs on the road. Yes, we have tried to educate them, but it is not working just yet. “See if it has an exhaust pipe. Does it have a sealed front?”

One car that I am seeing in ever increasing numbers is the refreshed Great Wall Motors ORA — now in an SUV body and a much cheaper price. When it launched back in 2023, I expected great things ( see our review here ). Sadly, the Funky Cat (as it is known in China) did not live up to expectations. It was the cheapest EV in Australia at the time (AU$46,000) but couldn’t compete with the BYD Dolphin and the MG 4. Now, relaunched as an SUV and with a more appropriate price (AU$34,000 — scratch that, just got an email that knocks another grand off the price), I am seeing them everywhere — 6 on the highway just yesterday.
So, on to the best-selling BEVs on the Australian market in October 2026:

Pretty much the same as last month. Obviously, BYD was the best-selling brand, closely followed by Tesla. BYD has six cars among the top twenty BEVs. There are no cars from Korean, Japanese, or European carmakers in the top ten BEV numbers. When all powertrains are considered, BYD is the second highest selling brand behind Toyota in the Australian market. There seems to be some talk in the auto news about Tesla and BYD being considered “legacy” brands — who would have thought?

raw_summary: WASHINGTON D.C. — More than 300 solar and storage companies are urging Congress to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), S. 5653, warning that outdated federal permitting processes and grid infrastructure bottlenecks are delaying critical energy projects and driving up electricity costs. In a letter to congressional leaders , the companies call on lawmakers to quickly send the bipartisan legislation to the President’s desk. The signatories note that solar and storage account for 70% of new electricity capacity added to the grid thus far in 2026, while $120 billion in clean energy investment remains caught in permitting delays.

article_paragraphs: WASHINGTON D.C. — More than 300 solar and storage companies are urging Congress to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), S. 5653, warning that outdated federal permitting processes and grid infrastructure bottlenecks are delaying critical energy projects and driving up electricity costs.

In a letter to congressional leaders , the companies call on lawmakers to quickly send the bipartisan legislation to the President’s desk. The signatories note that solar and storage account for 70% of new electricity capacity added to the grid thus far in 2026, while $120 billion in clean energy investment remains caught in permitting delays.

“You can’t lower energy costs if you can’t build the energy projects, and these companies know that this bipartisan legislation will help get America building again,” said Tim Pawlenty, CEO of the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA).

BAAJA would modernize the federal permitting system by ensuring fair treatment for all technologies, protecting lawfully issued permits from politically motivated delays, establishing predictable timelines for federal reviews and judicial proceedings, modernizing transmission planning, and expanding distributed energy resources’ access to wholesale electricity markets.

New SEIA analysis shows that BAAJA could unlock 167 gigawatts of additional solar capacity between 2028 and 2035, bringing solar to over 18% of U.S. electricity generation by 2035. The analysis finds that the bill’s reforms could reduce cumulative power sector CO2 emissions by approximately 20% and avoid $54 billion in public health damages.

The message from more than 300 companies comes as voters made clear in the midterm elections that lowering energy costs is a top concern. Permitting reform is urgently needed to meet rising demand and get more reliable, affordable solar and storage projects built.

About SEIA®: The Solar Energy Industries Association® (SEIA) is leading the transformation to a clean energy economy. SEIA works with its 1,200 member companies and other strategic partners to fight for policies that create jobs in every community and shape fair market rules that promote competition and the growth of reliable, low-cost solar power. Founded in 1974, SEIA is the national trade association for the solar and solar + storage industries, building a comprehensive vision for the Solar+ Decade through research, education and advocacy. Visit SEIA online at www.seia.org and follow @SEIA on Twitter , LinkedIn , and Instagram .

article_paragraphs: Five years ago, the first Mustang Mach-E customers began adding something important to the Ford electric vehicle battery validation work: real-world ownership at scale.

As part of our quality process, design and validation engineering starts long before a vehicle reaches a customer. We model battery performance, run physical tests, expose packs to heat, cold, and charging profiles, and build in margin for demanding real-world conditions.

These rigorous quality tests are designed to help us understand how battery systems perform across a wide range of climates, charging behaviors, and driving conditions before customers get behind the wheel.

Then David Blenkle drove past 400,000 miles on the original battery in his 2022 Mustang Mach-E. He gave us a real-world example of what is possible — and begged the question of whether he’s an outlier or not.

His battery health has remained strong through unusually high-mileage use. His experience gave our team a chance to compare one exceptional ownership case with what we are seeing across the broader fleet.
The bigger question was if David’s experience reflected a broader pattern. So, we decided to look back at the Mustang Mach-E owners who started it all: The Class of 2021.

raw_title: Experience The Gales Of November With This Real-Time Great Lakes Simulator
title: Experience The Gales Of November With This Real-Time Great Lakes Simulator
raw_summary: The wreck of the SS Edmund Fitzgerald became a bit of a meme last year during the 50th anniversary of the disaster. Gen Zers rediscovered the great Gordon Lightfoot song and it was all over the interwebz. Those youths can now experience the thrill, terror and wonder of the Great Lakes firsthand with my new favorite obsession, the website In The Lakes ; a free site which shows you the real-time conditions on any one of the great lakes without tracking your data. Using buoys located on Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie, and Lake Ontario and honorable mention Lake St. Claire, In The Lake users can view a digital simulation of conditions. Different colors on the map represent real-time wave heights. As of the writing of this story, both Lake Superior and Lake Michigan are mostly red, indicative of choppy waters and waves reaching 10 feet or more. My first "Float" sent me just north of Sault Ste. Marie in Lake Superior where it was, predictably, cold, grey, and extra choppy — just the sort of thing the Edmund Fitz faced on that cold day in November, 1975.

Different colors on the map represent real-time wave heights. As of the writing of this story, both Lake Superior and Lake Michigan are mostly red, indicative of choppy waters and waves reaching 10 feet or more. My first "Float" sent me just north of Sault Ste. Marie in Lake Superior where it was, predictably, cold, grey, and extra choppy — just the sort of thing the Edmund Fitz faced on that cold day in November, 1975.

But it's not all rough seas and wind. Pick a calmer section of lake and spend a few hours of your work day sipping a beverage, listening to a radio that features local radio stations as well as multiple genre stations, or meditate. The meditate feature is fairly entertaining, with inspirational messages meant to resonant with folks from the Great Lakes. The last time I pressed it, a message popped up reading "Somewhere, someone's shoveling a driveway. Not you. Not today." Damn right.

But it's not just floaties. You can find the option to "Take the helm in these conditions." And the familiar lake scene will load with a kayak, schooner, or even a Coast Guard ice breaking ship. I tried out the kayak to see what it was like for my husband when he puttered around Lake Superior on his own kayak, a feat that nearly killed him. You can also dive the depths of the lakes, or write a message and pop it in a bottle, then set it into the lake and see where the real forecast takes it.

In the Experiences tab you can take on several adventures from repairing the Cort for sailing duties to Cruising the Soo Locks. There's also a plethora of adventures to go on. I opted for the Brigade to the Rendezvous, an 1815 canoe trip to deliver beaver furs to Fort William, a midway trading point between the Midwest and Montreal. Teachers can also find a dedicated hub with tons of resources to go over critical things related to the Great Lakes, appropriate for certain grade levels.

Or keep it simple and continue to enjoy the occasional float on one of the Great Lakes. You can use it to escape your kids as easily as educate them, after all. An extra click will allow your setting to reset (change) every five minutes without your interference. So relax, ride the waves, and beware the gales of November.

title: New KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo Debuts - AMT, 8.8-inch TFT, Offline Sat-Nav
raw_summary: KTM has unveiled the all-new 1390 Super Duke GT Evo at EICMA 2026, which is positioned above the standard 1390 Super Duke GT. The new model gets a range of exclusive features, while borrowing the 1,350 cc LC8 V-twin engine platform from the KTM 1390 Super Adventure S Evo. article_paragraphs: KTM has unveiled the all-new 1390 Super Duke GT Evo at EICMA 2026, which is positioned above the standard 1390 Super Duke GT. The new model gets a range of exclusive features, while borrowing the 1,350 cc LC8 V-twin engine platform from the KTM 1390 Super Adventure S Evo. KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo will go on sale across global markets in early 2027. Whether it will make its way to India remains to be seen.

Engineered for sport-touring, KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo gets an advanced AMT transmission. What’s even better is that users have the option to choose between fully automated operation or manual shifting. The latter may be preferred by experienced riders or in specific scenarios where more responsive feedback and greater manual control are needed.

With the AMT active, users don’t need to shift gears, making long distance sport-touring a lot less tiring. KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo uses a 1,350cc, 2-cylinder, V 75° engine, which is the same as in use with 1390 Super Adventure S Evo. It generates 187 hp and 145 Nm of peak torque.

KTM has introduced new features with the 1390 Super Duke GT Evo to enhance rider comfort and safety. For context, a more upright riding stance is possible with the forward-adjustable handlebars. Similarly, the windshield can be adjusted to low and high positions, as per requirement. The bike has a seat height of 834 mm. It weighs 213 kg and has 149 mm of ground clearance.

Latest-gen electronically-controlled WP Semi Active Technology (SAT) suspension has been used, with easy adjustability options via the dashboard. This suspension setup uses a new patented thru-rod construction, making it lighter than previous-gen versions. Riders benefit from a more precise and consistent response. Users can also adjust the hydraulic clutch and brake levers.

Frame stiffness has been improved and is now 3X higher than the standard model. Precision handling and front tyre feedback have been improved with more robust connections between the frame, forks, triple clamps and swingarm. The bike has enhanced stability and offers an optimized balance between comfort and sporty riding.

KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo has 17-inch wheels at both ends, wrapped in Michelin Power 6 tires. These are 120/70 at the front and 190/55 at the rear. The overall setup is 1.2 kg lighter and the tyres have special compounds that enhance straight line control and cornering grip. Braking setup comprises four-piston Brembo Stylema monoblock callipers with 320 mm floating discs at the front and a twin-piston floating calliper with a 240 mm disc at the rear.

KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo gets an 8.8-inch TFT display with an easy menu structure. It has full offline onboard map navigation and a USB Type-C charging port. The bike uses a new LED headlight setup, which has better near field illumination and a larger field of view up to 90 degrees.

raw_title: VW Compact SUV For India Arriving In 2027 – What We Know So Far
title: VW Compact SUV For India Arriving In 2027
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - New Volkswagen compact SUV will share its architecture with the Skoda Kylaq and could borrow design elements from the Taigun and Virtus The Volkswagen Polo disappeared from Indian showrooms in 2022 after the Ameo compact sedan had already been discontinued. The German manufacturer is now preparing a return to the sub-four-metre passenger vehicle category, this time in the form of an SUV. Volkswagen confirmed the new model a few months ago and has scheduled its market introduction for 2027. The vehicle will be developed and manufactured in India and it will sit below the Taigun as the most affordable SUV in the Volkswagen portfolio. The exterior could take inspiration from the recently updated Taigun and the Virtus facelift which is scheduled to arrive soon. The Taigun received revised LED headlights, illuminated Volkswagen emblems, a horizontal grille light bar and redesigned alloy wheels earlier this year. On a side note, the Virtus facelift’s bumpers, lighting elements, and GT detailing will see revisions. The compact SUV could feature a similar grille treatment, prominent wheel arches, distinctive LED daytime running lamps and a redesigned rear section. The closest mechanical relative of the new Volkswagen SUV will be the Skoda Kylaq. Both use the MQB A0 IN architecture developed by engineering teams in India and Europe. The Kylaq measures 3,995 mm in length and has a wheelbase of 2,566 mm. Similar proportions are likely for the Volkswagen derivative alongside common structural components, suspension bits and mechanical systems. Also Read: New Volkswagen Virtus Launching Soon : Top 5 changes To Expect Representational The shared platform also supports extensive localisation and manufacturing at the Volkswagen Group facility in Chakan. The compact SUV is expected to receive the 1.0-litre three-cylinder TSI turbo petrol engine used in the Kylaq. The motor kicks out 115 PS and 178 Nm in the Skoda SUV. The Kylaq currently offers a six-speed manual and a six-speed torque converter automatic gearbox. However, the Volkswagen derivative is tipped to receive an eight-speed automatic transmission. The interior could feature a 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment system, an 8-inch digital instrument cluster, wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay connectivity and automatic climate control. Other likely equipment are ventilated front seats, electric adjustment for the driver seat, wireless phone charging, cruise control and an electric sunroof. The Kylaq already offers many of these features but Volkswagen could introduce different dashboard materials, upholstery, display graphics and controls. Also Read: 5+ All-New Compact SUVs Arriving Soon In India – Maruti To Volkswagen Brazil-spec Volkswagen Tera A GT Line variant featuring dark exterior accents and unique interior trim is another possibility. As for safety, six airbags, electronic stability control, traction control, ABS, electronic brakeforce distribution, hill-hold assistance, ISOFIX child seat mounts and tyre pressure monitoring system will be available along with a reversing camera and parking sensors. The Skoda Kylaq has already secured five stars in Bharat NCAP safety tests. Volkswagen has confirmed that the platform will support safety systems suitable for Indian regulations. The Volkswagen compact SUV is expected to cost between Rs. 8 lakh and Rs. 13 lakh (ex-showroom). It will compete against the Tata Nexon, Maruti Suzuki Brezza, Hyundai Venue, Kia Sonet, Mahindra XUV 3XO and its Skoda counterpart.

title: New BYD Seal 07 Illustrates Chinese EV Evolution
raw_summary: Last week, BYD introduced the next generation Seal 07 EV. This model replaces the original BYD Seal, which entered the market in late 2022 and put the brand on the map in the minds of many people around the world. While the new vehicle is important to BYD, it also illustrates many of the changes that have happened to the EVs and the EV market in China over the past few years. That also makes it slightly larger than the late Tesla Model S.

article_paragraphs: Last week, BYD introduced the next generation Seal 07 EV. This model replaces the original BYD Seal, which entered the market in late 2022 and put the brand on the map in the minds of many people around the world. While the new vehicle is important to BYD, it also illustrates many of the changes that have happened to the EVs and the EV market in China over the past few years.

The new Seal 07 grows to 5080 mm long by 1960 mm wide by 1495 mm tall. That compares to 4,800 mm long, 1,875 mm wide and 1,460 mm high for the previous Seal. That also makes it slightly larger than the late Tesla Model S.

Like many new BYD cars, the interior has become more premium and technologically advanced. Interiors offer front zero gravity seats with heating, ventilation and massage. An onboard refrigerator is offered in the center console and a power sunshade in the roof. Speakers have proliferated. The screens have improved, programmable buttons can be added, and voice interaction has improved. Basic versions come with BYD’s God’s Eye C with BYD covering autonomous parking, while higher trims offer LiDAR-based God’s Eye B with BYD adding coverage for city navigation.

Seal 07 models now come with DiSus-C adaptive damping on lower trim models and DiSus-M magnetorheological active dampers on higher trims. Suspension is double wishbones up front, multilink at the rear.

Of course, the new car offers BYD’s flash charging, capable of charging from 10-70% in 5 minutes and 10-97% in 9 minutes, while taking 12 minutes to go from 10-97% at -30 C with no preconditioning. 20,000 BYD flash charging stations are planned to be in operation by the end of the year, which will be more than all DC charging stations in the US combined. Meanwhile, the previous Seal took 26 minutes to go from 30-80%.

Looking at the closest version of the original Seal from 2022, battery capacity has dropped from 82.5 kW to 76.4 kW for the new model. Meanwhile, range increased to 775 km CLTC from 700 km in the old model due to greater efficiency. While efficiency may have once been a criticism of the Seal, it is now a highlight. Power is up from 230 kW to 245 kW (329 hp). Meanwhile, a curb weight of 1975 kg is lighter than the previous 700 km model (2055 kg), with increased use of UHSS in the structure.

Overall, it is a larger and more luxurious car than the vehicle it replaces, while losing a little weight. Performance, charging and efficiency have improved. Equipment levels are higher. Technology is more advanced. And then we get to affordability.

In 2022, the original Seal offered a 550 km range trim for 209,800 RMB ($31,424 USD at current exchange rates), but the 700 km range version, which is closest to the new model, started at 259,800 RMB ($38,913).

raw_title: BYD Yangwang Altior Debuts – CNY 2 Million (Rs 2.9 Cr) Rolls Royce Phantom Rival
title: BYD Yangwang Altior Debuts - CNY 2 Million (Rs 2.9 Cr) Rolls Royce Phantom Rival
raw_summary: BYD’s ultra luxury flagship sub brand, Yangwang , has unveiled its new all-electric flagship sedan – the Altior. While the name comes from the Latin word ‘Altior’ meaning ‘higher’, the sedan’s exterior and interior elements are inspired by popular design concepts in Chinese culture and craftsmanship. Yangwang Altior sets new benchmarks in the electric luxury segment and will primarily challenge rivals such as the Rolls-Royce Phantom. Inspiration for BYD Yangwang Altior’s design comes from the ‘ding’, which is an ancient Chinese ceremonial bronze vessel. Key features include a jewelled grille that creates dynamic visual compositions as light reflects off its surface. LED headlamps and DRLs follow a distinctive setup, inspired by the Yangwang logo. The lighting setup comes alive sequentially as the owner approaches, ensuring an engaging ceremonial welcome.

Yangwang Altior uses large 21-inch wheels, wrapped in 275/45 low-noise tyres. Users can choose from three distinct designs for the wheels. The sedan has coach-style doors, with the front units opening 80 degrees and the rear ones a full 90 degrees. 2nd-row doors are rear hinged, further improving easy ingress and egress. All doors have bespoke umbrellas, which are inspired by the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at China’s Temple of Heaven complex.

Altior sedan has a commanding presence, contributed partly by its large size. It is 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, 1,590 mm tall and has a wheelbase of 3,500 mm. The model showcased has a dual-tone finish, combining bronze and a darker shade on the bonnet and roof.

Inside, the Yangwang Altior uses premium materials and exquisite finishes. Yellow Hetian jade material used for the air-vent detailing conveys a deep cultural significance. Similarly, the upholstery features Suzhou embroidery with precision perforation. Jewellery-inspired elements have been used liberally across the cabin, including various controls.

Real metal switches have been used to ensure a more precise tactile response. These metal components also have the desired aural experience, having been thoroughly tested for their sound output. Other key highlights include pure wool floor mats, full grain semi-aniline leather and natural wood accents on the dashboard and doors.

The dashboard features a largely full-width touchscreen, flanked by vertically stacked AC vents. Yangwang Altior is a 4-seater sedan and is equipped with aviation-style zero-gravity seats in the second row. These have a dedicated massage system, powered by four ball-shaped massage heads.

Rear passengers have 354 mm of knee room and 1,209 mm of legroom. Users can set the right mood with lighting, sound and fragrance. A 39-speaker Dynaudio Platinum Evidence audio system has been used for an immersive experience. The sedan also has a powered 21.4-inch overhead screen, which can be used for entertainment and conference calls. Compact refrigerators are provided at the front and rear. The sedan has a boot space of 532 litres.

Naturally, as with many other well-to-do star athletes, he has a penchant for flashy cars. Problem is, he seldom fits in them without some contortions and modification. It's what drove him to have a Lamborghini lengthened into a Franken-Gallardo . That stretched supercar isn't the only time Shaq did some silly stuff with expensive cars.

In what was almost certainly a prideful purchase, O'Neal bought three outrageously expensive cars on the spot. Why? All it took was one condescending question from a less-than-respectful Rolls-Royce dealership salesman, and Shaq bought the lot. Just like that, the champ and business mogul had three extra opulent cars he says "I never drive."

Don't believe it? One of them, a 2004 Rolls-Royce Phantom, just sold on Bring-a-Trailer. If that wasn't enough, the once-undisputed heavyweight champion of the world, Mike Tyson, may have had a hand in nudging the Diesel to buy three ultraluxe cars instead of a solitary sedan. Of course, it's not difficult to get carried away when shopping for Rolls-Royces; just look at the one-off Phantom inspired by "Goldfinger."

Some 30 years ago, Shaquille O'Neal signed a groundbreaking $120 million deal to don Los Angeles Lakers colors and put away his Orlando Magic jersey. Several years later, he wandered into a Rolls-Royce showroom with his friend Alex and started browsing the hand-built grandeur.

Now, O'Neal had money to spare, but he wasn't quite up for indiscriminate spending. "I like to spend money, but I don't like to waste money. So I don't want to spend $400,000 for a car," O'Neal recalled in a Revolt interview. He went about asking a salesperson about the prices of the showroom's many Roll-Royces. That's when the salesperson said the wrong thing. Or the right thing, considering the commission on three hilariously expensive cars.

In O'Neal's book, "Shaq Uncut: My Story," he recalls the question as especially disrespectful, be it accidental or deliberate. The salesperson gave the Lakers sweatpants-clad O'Neal a glance and, per Basketball Network , asked, "Are you sure you can afford it, sonny boy?" That did it. Shaq lost it. "I said, 'What the f*** did you just say to me?'" So, he pointed around the showroom. "I want that silver hardtop one, and I want the green one, and give that red one over there, too."

One of those cars, the silver hardtop O'Neal selected, was a 2004 Rolls-Royce Phantom. That car sold in November 2026 on Bring-a-Trailer for $62,000. Not exactly the $320,000 or so O'Neal likely paid for it when it was new in 2004. Although he was shopping in a Rolls-Royce dealer, Shaq's book mentions a handful of Bentleys as part of the splurge. Whichever British luxury marque made O'Neal's list of picks, it was quite the spendy visit to a dealership.

Shaq's financial flexing and what is likely the most impressive commission that Rolls-Royce salesperson has ever made makes for a pretty crazy story. Believe it or not, it gets even more wild from there. According to O'Neal's book, "Iron" Mike himself, Mike Tyson, was in the mood for Bentley shopping just as the Laker found himself at the dealership.

In 1925 Albert L. Luce, who owned Ford dealerships in Fort Valley and Perry, Georgia, sold a customer a bus to carry workers to a cement plant. He had mounted a locally-made wooden body onto a Ford Model TT truck chassis, but the body started rattling apart on rural Georgia roads before the customer had even finished paying for it. It was a disaster.
This is a 1986 Blue Bird Wanderlodge, it’s one of the most luxurious motorhomes of its time, and this example benefits from $110,000+ spent on renovations and upgrades in the last few years.

Luce was completely convinced he could build a better bus, and by 1927 he’d done it. It had a body of steel sheet, as well as wood and canvas over a steel framework, on a Model TT chassis with Ford’s 177 cubic inch (2.9 liter) four-cylinder rated at 20 bhp.

The new bus went to Frank Slade of Marshallville, Georgia, who used it to carry schoolchildren. Many years later, Luce’s son Albert “Buddy” Luce Jr. bought the bus back for the sake of posterity, and he later donated it to The Henry Ford Museum in Dearborn in 2008. It’s now the oldest surviving school bus in America.

Buses remained a sideline for the company until the Great Depression gutted car sales in the 1930s, Luce sold his dealership and in 1932 founded the Blue Bird Body Company in Fort Valley, about 25 miles south of Macon, Georgia.

According to the company’s official history, he rejected his own surname as the company name for fear of jokes about a “loose bus,” and took the new name after schoolchildren likened one of his blue-and-yellow buses to a little bluebird. A dedicated 27,000 square foot factory opened in 1935, and Blue Bird built its first all-steel bus in 1937. By the end of the Second World War it ranked 7th among 12 American school bus makers.

title: Sierra Club Welcomes CalPERS' $71 Billion Climate-Solutions Investment Milestone, Urges Fund to End Financing of Fossil Fuel Expansion
raw_summary: SACRAMENTO, CA — On Monday, the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) reported that the value of investments it classifies as climate solutions reached $71 billion as of June 30, 2026, up from $59.7 billion a year earlier. The increase brings the nation’s largest public pension fund closer to its goal of $100 billion in climate investments by 2030. Sierra Club welcomed CalPERS’ continued commitment to climate-solutions investing and called on the fund to adopt stronger standards and transparency around what counts toward its $100 billion goal. Sierra Club also urged CalPERS to prioritize investments that support real-world emissions reductions and address climate risks across its broader portfolio to protect the retirement security of the workers and retirees it serves.
summary: SACRAMENTO, CA — On Monday, the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) reported that the value of investments it classifies as climate solutions reached $71 billion as of June 30, 2026, up from $59.7 billion a year earlier. The increase brings the nation’s largest public pension fund closer to its goal of $100 billion in climate investments by 2030.
article_paragraphs: SACRAMENTO, CA — On Monday, the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) reported that the value of investments it classifies as climate solutions reached $71 billion as of June 30, 2026, up from $59.7 billion a year earlier. The increase brings the nation’s largest public pension fund closer to its goal of $100 billion in climate investments by 2030.

Sierra Club welcomed CalPERS’ continued commitment to climate-solutions investing and called on the fund to adopt stronger standards and transparency around what counts toward its $100 billion goal. Sierra Club also urged CalPERS to prioritize investments that support real-world emissions reductions and address climate risks across its broader portfolio to protect the retirement security of the workers and retirees it serves.
In response, Ben Cushing, Director of Sierra Club’s Sustainable Finance Campaign, released the following statement:

“It’s encouraging to see CalPERS make progress toward its climate-solutions goal, but a growing investment total doesn’t tell us how much new money is helping build clean energy and cut emissions. Reducing climate risk also means looking at where CalPERS invests across the whole portfolio. CalPERS has already taken the important step of using its votes to hold company directors accountable for how they handle climate risk. It can build on that work by adopting a policy to stop financing fossil fuel expansion and backing climate projects that need new investment to get built or expand.”

CalPERS said the $11.3 billion increase came from both new investments and gains on assets it already held. CalPERS also reported that financed emissions across the asset classes covered by its analysis rose by approximately 6 percent over the past year, largely reflecting investments in higher-emitting assets that it expects to decarbonize over time. For its global public equity and U.S. corporate credit holdings, CalPERS reported an implied temperature rise of 2.9°C, up from 2.7°C a year earlier.

Last year, Sierra Club and the California Common Good coalition urged CalPERS to publish a full list of the investments it counts toward its $100 billion goal, adopt science-based standards for what qualifies as a climate solution, and exclude fossil fuel investments from that total. Sierra Club has raised these concerns at CalPERS board meetings, and elaborated on them in a December 2025 CalMatters op-ed questioning the credibility and real-world impact of CalPERS’ reported climate investments.

Sierra Club’s 2025 Principles for Climate Solutions Investments outline standards for credible investing, including prioritizing real-world emissions reductions and establishing safeguards for transition financing. Its January 2026 Climate Solutions Gap report likewise highlighted CalPERS as an example of why ambitious climate-solutions targets must be backed by credible definitions, clear eligibility criteria, and transparent reporting.

article_paragraphs: EAST HAMPTON, Connecticut — On Saturday, November 7, Sierra Club Connecticut supporters, other community groups, and allies walked for four hours across seven miles from Hurd State Park to Eversource Headquarters in East Hampton to protest the utility’s proposed Southeast Resilience Pipeline. Fifty people attended the Walk to Stop the SERPent Pipeline . Of the 50, 37 participated in the seven-mile walk to Eversource Headquarters.

Sierra Club and partner organizations have given the proposed Eversource pipeline the name “SERPent” to highlight its potential harm to public health, energy affordability, climate, and the Connecticut River which, if approved, the pipeline will run under.

“Prioritizing profit over the health of the environment is to our own detriment,” said Erin Day, Owner of Ten Summit Yoga and Earth Based Wellness. “ Protecting our natural landscapes is essential, as the connection to the earth is what sustains our own well-being. Preserving this land from the pipeline is a vital step in honoring our relationship with nature and upholding our responsibility for a healthy future.”

“Building communities resilient to climate and economic crises requires improving people’s health and environments while preventing the danger and destruction posed by this pipeline and similar projects,” said Diana Martinez, of Chicks Ahoy Farm. “We can’t allow our futures to be sacrificed for corporate gain.”

“Eversource wants to build a pipeline under the Connecticut River because they make more money building pipelines than they do selling gas; they are a for profit company making a billion IN PROFIT per year so we know what their priorities are,” said Martha Klein, Sierra Club Connecticut and the No Pipeline Expansion Northeast Coalition. “Eversource is blocking the transition to the modern energy economy by expanding fracked gas infrastructure in our state, which locks us into methane use for decades. Burning fossil gas kills people, disrupts the climate and makes energy unaffordable, but it has been very profitable for Eversource. The time for change is here.”

“As young people, we are critically aware of the fallacies embedded in the short-term logic of fossil fuel infrastructure,” said Jo Almond, Sunrise Movement Wesleyan. “I grew up in a town with one hundred and forty-four active methane gas leaks; a result of relying on natural gas pipelines imposed by our utility company. I want to be part of the last generation who has to deal with the toxicity that fossil fuels introduce into our communities; this pipeline would guarantee that Connecticut’s youth will be growing up alongside poisoned water, air, and soil for generations to come.”

“Environmental racism harms all communities and it is important to hold corporations and utilities accountable for expanding poisonous methane gas into our communities and exposing us to environmental harms that exacerbate health, housing, education and economic barriers,” said Tenaya Taylor, Nonprofit Accountability Group.

title: Humble Hauler autonomous trailer takes the truck out of trucking [update]
raw_summary: Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the company’s transition from prototype to preproduction. The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble said it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

article_paragraphs: Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the company’s transition from prototype to preproduction.

The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble said it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

“We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO , Eyal Cohen. “The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day.”
We originally covered the Humble Hauler back in May. You can check out the original article, below, then let us know what you think of the company’s prospects in the comments.

The startup that dares to ask, “Why does the Macbook driving my freight around need a whole cab?” just showed off a fully driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform designed to handle containerized cargo more efficiently than ever.

Instead of looking at the tractor and asking how to make it work without a driver , Humble looked at the trailer, itself, redesigning the container chassis as a vehicle from the ground up . The end result isn’t just an autonomous solution, it’s an overall lighter platform without a cab that saves shippers the weight of a sleeper cab, a day cab, or the truck at all.
The Humble approach is said to improve payload efficiency of shipping containers, and intended for dock-to-dock operation .

“I have dedicated my career to building electric and autonomous vehicle technology,” explains Eyal Cohen, Humble Robotics’ founder and CEO. “For the first time, freight can be fully automated all the way to the loading dock. article_paragraphs: PlugShare is giving its EV charging app a big overhaul. Version 8.0 arrives worldwide for iPhone on November 10, with dark mode, a trip planner that shows how far apart charging stops are, and a rebuilt Apple Watch app that can point you to a charger compatible with your EV.

Dark mode was one of the most-requested features from PlugShare users. It works across the app and follows your iPhone’s settings, so if your phone switches to dark mode at sunset, your charging map will, too.

The trip planner gets a small but handy change. Each charging stop now shows how far it is from both the start of your trip and the previous stop. So when you’re deciding whether to stretch to the next fast charger or stop sooner, the number you need is right there.

PlugShare now loads your saved locations, trips, and profile when you open the app or sign in, so those tabs are ready to tap. You can also open and zoom in on station photos right from their thumbnails. That’s handy when you’re trying to figure out what corner a charging station is in in a big parking lot. The app also adapts its layout to the iPhone Duo’s different screens and folded positions.

The rebuilt Watch app lists nearby charging stations with distances and directions. It uses the filters you’ve set on your iPhone, so if you’ve filtered for plugs that fit your EV, that carries over to your wrist.

Tap a station and you’ll see its PlugScore, the network that runs it, a small map, and which plugs it has, including NACS, CCS, CHAdeMO, or J1772. The list refreshes when you raise your wrist and open the app. You can also add a shortcut to a round or corner slot on your watch face.
The iPhone update is rolling out through the App Store . PlugShare says Android users will get dark mode and a redesign based on Google’s Material 3 in early 2027.

title: The All-Electric Optiq Marks Cadillac's Return To Australia
raw_summary: From the early 1930s until 1969, Cadillac was once a household name in Australia. Luxury buyers could sample several of its models made their way Down Under, including the classic Eldorado. After that, the brand disappeared from local shores. summary: From the early 1930s until 1969, Cadillac was once a household name in Australia. Luxury buyers could sample several of its models made their way Down Under, including the classic Eldorado. After that, the brand disappeared from local shores.
article_paragraphs: From the early 1930s until 1969, Cadillac was once a household name in Australia. Luxury buyers could sample several of its models made their way Down Under, including the classic Eldorado. After that, the brand disappeared from local shores.

Speaking to a crowd at the Australian launch of Cadillac's new Formula 1 team in Melbourne back in March, which I attended, GM president Mark Reuss said the automaker had come close to relaunching Cadillac in Australia in the early 2000s, but the plan ultimately fell through. In the late 2010s, I even spotted several camouflaged prototypes testing , as the brand again toyed with the idea of returning. Now, Cadillac is officially back, albeit as an EV-only brand.

Rather than selling gas-guzzling models like the Escalade or the CT5-V Blackwing in Australia, Cadillac has launched with the Optiq , Lyriq, and Vistiq. We recently spent a week with the Optiq, eager to see if it has any hope of rivaling competitors from Asia and Europe, and were pleasantly surprised with what we found.

Just a single version of the Optiq is available locally, known as the Sport AWD. It uses a 75-kWh nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) battery and dual motors producing 224 kW (300 hp) and 480 Nm (354 lb-ft) of torque. Like the American version, Australia's right-hand drive Optiq is manufactured in Mexico. The Optiq was updated in the U.S. for 2026 with new powertrains, including a rear-wheel drive model and a more powerful all-wheel drive version, but these versions have yet to arrive in Australia.

Prices start at AU$85,000 ($59,700) before options but including fees. At that price, it sounds like quite a good deal, especially when compared to the smaller, entry-level Audi Q4 45 e-tron, which starts at AU$93,173 ($65,500) including fees. It's also cheaper than the new Volvo EX60 starting at AU$86,000 ($60,500) before fees, and upwards of AU$94,000 ($66,000) with fees. Unsurprisingly, the Optiq does struggle on price when compared to some premium Chinese offerings like the Zeekr 7X, priced from AU$79,749 ($56,000) for the far more powerful and better-equipped Performance AWD.

The Optiq's highlight is definitely the interior. Ever since Tesla released the game-changing Model 3 a decade ago, many other brands have adopted similar ultra-minimalistic philosophies when designing the cabins of new models. The Chinese are especially fond of this approach, resulting in cars from different brands that seem to have almost identical interiors. The Cadillac is different.

First are the screens, or should I say, the single 33-inch curved display found in other Cadillac models. It's a welcome reprieve from the tablet-like screens we've grown accustomed to, looking like a piece of high-end jewelry compared to them. The screen doesn't only look the part, but it performs exceptionally well, too, and includes wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. It also includes Google Built-in with the Google Assistant and Google Maps.

Cadillac also deserves praise for the materials used throughout the cabin. There's plush leatherette upholstery on the seats and parts of the doors, as well as a lovely fabric material on the doors and the floating center console, made from recycle polyethylene. The Optiq also includes metal AKG speaker grilles, knurled metal around the cupholders, and volume dial, as well as metal toggles for the climate control. The choice of materials distinguishes the Optiq from its competitors and gives it the high-end feel you'd expect from a Cadillac.

After that, the brand disappeared from local shores.

It’s safe to say we’re smitten with the way the E-class drives, an ideal blend of comfort and liveliness. If we had one nit to pick it would be the slight impact harshness from the 20-inch wheels and tires and their relatively shallow sidewalls. We’d probably like the ride better with the base 18-inch wheel-and-tire package and its additional sidewall, although it’s a major visual downgrade.

The E450 drives so well, and its 375-hp turbo inline-six is so smooth and melodious, that we’d be more than willing to overlook so-so fuel economy. But the E-class continues to impress there, too, with an overall average of 27 mpg, one better than its EPA combined figure. And that’s with a lot of heavy-footed commuting and not all that many road trips. On longer drives, we’ve seen well over 30 mpg.

Fall’s cooler temperatures have us in a warm glow about the E450’s not only heated steering wheel and seats (both pretty common nowadays) but also the heated center and outboard armrests, part of the $2950 Multicontour Seating package—decadent, perhaps, but a lovely way to start your commute on a chilly morning.

Our primary complaints tend to be about anything but the driving, including the touch-sensitive controls on the steering wheel, the door handles that sometimes don’t power out of the body quick enough, or the fingerprint-prone piano-black interior trim and vast array of three screens across the interior. We’ve also gotten plenty cross with the virtual assistant, which chimes in with obnoxious frequency if left to its automatic setting, interrupting conversations about everything from building developments in the area to the price of an item discussed. We quickly switched it back to having to hear the “Hey, Mercedes” wake phrase before inserting itself.

Mercedes specifies service for the E-class every 10,000 miles or 12 months, with the first one a simple oil change and various inspections. summary: The new Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past. Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan , including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.
article_paragraphs: The new Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.
Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan , including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.

While that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test , the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.

The EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.
During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.

The new EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.
Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.

raw_title: IIHS Founder Warned Drivers About The Dangers Of Speed Almost A Decade Before He Started The Organization: What's Streaming
title: IIHS Founder Warned Drivers About The Dangers Of Speed Almost A Decade Before He Started The Organization: What's Streaming
raw_summary: Not long before the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety was informing drivers of how dangerous or safe a car was , James S. Kemper was on a mission to improve road safety. Kemper worked in the insurance world in his first job out of high school. He was an "office boy" for Central Mutual Insurance according to his New York Times obituary , but he went on to produce his own driver safety materials: educational films. The films were made by Kemper's personal insurance company, Lumbermen Mutual Casualty, and in partnership with the LAPD and Traffic Safety Films Inc. The LAPD connection helped bring "Sergeant Bruce" to the films, who starred on-camera several times as the presenter of important safety lessons — each video with its own specific theme. Maybe it's Sgt. Bruce's personality, or maybe it's a cop-thing, but he also delivers a pseudo 1950s-version of scared straight energy with every specific dangerous driving situation.
summary: Not long before the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety was informing drivers of how dangerous or safe a car was , James S. Kemper was on a mission to improve road safety. Kemper worked in the insurance world in his first job out of high school.
article_paragraphs: Not long before the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety was informing drivers of how dangerous or safe a car was , James S. Kemper was on a mission to improve road safety. Kemper worked in the insurance world in his first job out of high school. He was an "office boy" for Central Mutual Insurance according to his New York Times obituary , but he went on to produce his own driver safety materials: educational films.

The films were made by Kemper's personal insurance company, Lumbermen Mutual Casualty, and in partnership with the LAPD and Traffic Safety Films Inc. The LAPD connection helped bring "Sergeant Bruce" to the films, who starred on-camera several times as the presenter of important safety lessons — each video with its own specific theme. Maybe it's Sgt. Bruce's personality, or maybe it's a cop-thing, but he also delivers a pseudo 1950s-version of scared straight energy with every specific dangerous driving situation.
Join me as I introduce a new(er), sometimes nostalgic video worth adding to your Watch Later lists. Leave a note in the comments if you find an older or interesting film you'd like to see featured.

In " Speed, The Accident Multiplier ," a film restored and posted by 16mm Time Machine on YouTube, the on-camera narrator, Sergeant Bruce of the LAPD, explains to viewers that speed is dangerous. He uses charts and figures to show how faster speed increases stopping distances. The biggest takeaway is that the faster you go, the longer it takes to brake, and the more likely the damage to whatever the car hits will be catastrophic. That same messaging carried over into the IIHS organization decades later.

Sgt. Bruce ended the film in a familiar way that you'll find with most of these films: A message about how engaging with these dangers will lead to death. In "Speed," he tells viewers, "Speeding is a two-edged sword. It makes an accident more probable, and at the same time, it makes death more certain." He went on to explain that one out of every three fatal accidents involved a speeding driver, "which means in one out of three cases, a driver took a chance with death and lost."

There are a couple more films Kemper and his organizations had made in 1950 that are also available on YouTube. The next two, or rather four, were uploaded by PeriscopeFilm — specifically, they're two short double-features. The first pairs " Following Too Close " and " Driver Irritations ," with the second pairing including "Child Safety" and "Driver or Pedestrian" — with the latter admittedly sounding more like a dangerous game, and that was likely the point. The opening to "Driver or Pedestrian" doesn't mess around either. Within the first minute, a camera follows a man driving a car as Sgt. Bruce tells viewers, "This is a driver..." before cutting to a tombstone, where Sgt. Bruce adds, "...who was a pedestrian. This is how it happened." Quite a way to set the scene.

Nine years later, Kemper's company joined forces with another two insurance companies to form the IIHS. Another decade after that, the IIHS would become its own scientific research organization, conducting studies to better understand road safety and finding ways to help improve it. By that point, IIHS had begun to do its own vehicle safety testing, as well. Those tests — although they have changed some as vehicles have evolved quite a bit since the 1960s — still provide consumers with important information regarding the safety of their vehicles today, like its latest look into the safety of heavy-duty trucks and cargo vans .

Kemper's work in insurance also helped push mutual insurance to the forefront in the U.S. , which, if you're unfamiliar, it means the insurance company is owned by policyholders. There are no stock shareholders to appease. He was adamant about ensuring people were paid for their claims. In his New York Times obituary, he's quoted saying, "I made up my mind that this company was going to settle claims for cash in the shortest time possible. I did not see then and do not see now the value of contesting claims you know you will settle." Anyone feel like a few insurance companies could take some notes? Kemper's legacy endures with his insurance company over a century later, which now exists as Kemper Insurance, and the place where he left the biggest mark — in his role establishing the IIHS.

Not two weeks later, the town's police department found not only were the cameras still on, but they continued to record vehicles, using infrared technology for the dark trash-bag induced conditions.

Excelsior Springs Police Department took to Facebook on November 5 to inform its residents of the issue. The department's Lieutenant Ryan Dowdy told Local 12 that the city initially placed bags over the cameras when they voted to end its contract with Flock and remove the cameras. However, not only are the cameras still on, the black garbage bags do not seem to block Flock's automated license plate reader's infrared technology. The company touts that tech on its own website as "nighttime performance that doesn't quit."
Also problematic is that with a cancelled contract the police department cannot access or use the data but other law enforcement agencies might be able to.

The 15 cameras installed in the town have recorded some vehicles, Dowdy said that most of these images have been headlights and taillights, with a few license plates. The screenshot image shared to Excelsior Springs Police Department's Facebook page showed a few of the vehicles captured through the garbage bags with the infrared. The third of the semi-hazy images showed a red box over the license plate it captured.

About a month ago, the police department held an informative session with the people of Excelsior Springs to explain Flock's ALPR technology to citizens. Community concerns still prevailed in taking down the cameras, as the council voted unanimously a couple of weeks later to cancel the contract. Although the police department said not using the 15 cameras posted in town will affect its police work, Dowdy said it continues efforts to be honest with area residents.
"You know, we'd rather tell people, be upfront about it," Dowdy said. "We're not trying to hide anything. To be honest, we haven't looked at it until yesterday to even find that it was occurring."

The city's solution for now is to double-bag the cameras until they are removed, hopefully some time around the contract's end at the end of this month. This latest folly is another warning to towns, cities and communities that have gone about covering their cameras with trash bags to double up. Who knows what kind of trash can seep through just the one layer.

title: Disney Testing AI-Powered 'Cars'-Themed Parking Assistants
raw_summary: Your next trip to Disneyland may look a little different. The Walt Disney Company has revealed it is testing AI-powered robot assistants that will help drivers find a parking space at the company's crowded resorts. Finding a convenient parking space at a Disneyland resort can be stressful for even the most patient drivers, so these robots could be a godsend. How Disney plans to protect them from rogue drivers remains to be seen. These robots — inspired by "Cars" and "Wall-E" characters — were previewed during the recent Disney Accelerator Demo Day. They are being tested in partnership with Field AI, a robotics firm founded in 2023 with former staff from Google's DeepMind, NASA, Nvidia, Tesla, and others. While a lot of focus in the robotics field is on advanced humanoid robots similar to those from Tesla, Boston Dynamics, and several Chinese firms, these parking assistants haven't been designed to look like a person.

They are being tested in partnership with Field AI, a robotics firm founded in 2023 with former staff from Google's DeepMind, NASA, Nvidia, Tesla, and others. While a lot of focus in the robotics field is on advanced humanoid robots similar to those from Tesla, Boston Dynamics, and several Chinese firms, these parking assistants haven't been designed to look like a person.

Instead, one of the small robots previewed is a tiny four-wheeler not dissimilar to some of the self-driving food delivery robots used in the U.S. One of these robots was shown painted bright orange and with bright yellow accents to mimic a fluorescent vest. It then includes a large screen in place of a traditional windshield, complete with eyes that move and active eyelids, just like the beloved characters from "Cars."

Positioned atop of the autonomous robot's roof is a changing sign that points drivers in the direction of a parking space. Additionally, the robot includes two small arms with red lights to also guide drivers, much like an aircraft marshaller. The robots look very cute, but we suspect they're also very expensive. With stressed parents trying to park and excitable kids in the backseat, we suspect more than a few of these parking assistant robots could be hit, either accidentally or intentionally.

Disney hasn't provided any timeline as to when these robotic parking assistants could be deployed, nor has it guaranteed that they will indeed be deployed at Disneyland locations. While they may be less prone to errors than human parking assistants, the initial outlay on them won't come cheap. We'd hate to think how much the cost of these robots will add to the prices of Disney's already-ballooning admission rates — the average cost for a family of four to get into the park costs between $476 and $836.

raw_summary: Ever since Skipp Sudduth asked for “Something very Fast. Audi S8. Something that can shove a little bit,” in 1998's Ronin , Audi's big body sedan has been the stuff of legend. Mercedes-Benz S-Class ? Too obvious. BMW 7-Series ? You don't want to look like a wannabe James Bond. But an Audi A8? That's what you drive when you have a nickname like The Transporter . Thus, Audi has just pressed pause on production of the A8, with no immediate plans in place to reboot it.

The Neckarsulm plant where the A8 was being built has already pivoted to production of the Audi A5 in both sedan and Avant forms, in standard and S5 or RS5 trims. Audi has been headquartered in Ingolstadt since the 1980s, long enough to have that city be shorthand for the company the way Stuttgart is for Porsche, but the Neckarsulm plant has roots stretching back to the nineteenth century via NSU, one of the companies that ended up forming Audi's four rings

Launched in 1994, the A8 arrived with aluminum-intensive construction to keep weight down and an available 4.2-liter V8 that still rates as one of the best-sounding engines ever made. It was businesslike, composed with all-wheel-drive for all conditions, managing to be both discreet and muscular, like a bodyguard in a well-tailored suit.

Subsequent generations remained a little more understated than rivals from Mercedes and BMW, but the fifth-gen car that's just exited production was only a year away from celebrating its tenth birthday. Even with a mid-cycle facelift, that's a bit long in the tooth for a flagship.

Taking over flagship duties is Audi's Q9 SUV, a proper three-row family hauler that's aimed at the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS . The Q9 is certainly large and imposing, and it can carry more passengers and cargo than any A8 model. Does it have that same charisma? Put it this way: Jason Bateman is a very talented actor and producer. He is not Jason Statham.

Meanwhile, Audi may return with some kind of electrified successor to the A8, perhaps as an extended, embiggened version of whatever the new battery-electric A4 ends up looking like. Until then, any Audi-loving underworld soldiers of fortune will have to make do with a brown Mercedes 450 SEL 6.9 and a rocket launcher.

OK, so we've seen that spending time living with an EV , even temporarily, goes a long way to debunking pro-oil propaganda and can change people's minds about whether or not an EV is right for them. Personally, I think the easiest way to make that happen is for owners who want to see EVs get more popular to lend their cars to as many people as they can, for at least 3 days at a time. Ideally, automakers would offer 120-hour test drives to anyone who wants one, but that would be wildly expensive, so I understand why it's hard to even get a 72-hour loan.

Automakers can't sit back here, though. And I'm not just saying that because EVs are the future (they really are), or because I want my nieces and nephews to grow up breathing clean air (I really do). No, it's because they're already shipping EVs to the U.S., and selling more of them would help both sales and profits, while keeping excess inventory from piling up on dealer lots. So here's the idea I'm offering every automaker, free and clear: introduce incentives that encourage dealers to use EVs as service loaners.

When an auto journalist gives business advice, usually, the best thing any automaker can do is the opposite. And that goes double when that advice is on Jalopnik, a site that still loves a good s—post. I'm also well aware I'm not a serious journalist. But tell me the service loaner isn't the most cost-effective way to get customers into an EV long enough for them to realize how great it is to have a gas station in your garage.

I know we all love conquest sales, but current owners are your most likely future customers. The real key to a future EV sale, though, is the low-pressure, no-commitment, just-try-it-for-fun nature of the service loaner. Even people who actively hate EVs would probably be willing to play with one for three or four days while their car's in the shop if the loaner was free. Customers are less likely to think it's some sort of sales trick, too, if the offer comes from a service manager instead of a salesperson.

Considering we're talking about people who already own a car, I don't know if we'd see large numbers of owners picking up their cars, handing over the keys to the loaner EV, and demanding to trade their car in. But as long as you make a good car, there are no downsides to making a positive impression on your customers. And I bet that program would end up being the most cost-effective sales tool in any automaker's arsenal. Not because they're forcing people to go electric but because EVs do such a great job of selling themselves when they fit a prospective owner's lifestyle.

Not everyone can justify an EV. It's pricier and less convenient if you can't charge at home, and some people do crazy amounts of driving or frequent towing. But if you work for an automaker, you know your EVs make better daily drivers for regular homeowners than your most popular daily drivers, and you know they'd sell better if you could get more butts in seats. Now you have a way to get your most likely customers' butts in those seats for far less than the cost of launching a 120-hour test drive program.

Even better, the anti-EV crowd should be all over this one. If EVs are still as bad as they're convinced they are, then a few days driving an EV should be all anyone needs to disabuse them of the notion that they should go electric. Give the skeptics at your company the opportunity to rack up a win and prove this whole EV thing is a waste of everyone's time and money. I mean, they aren't afraid people will like EVs better if they just spend some time with one, are they? Let's put our money where our mouth is and find out.

raw_title: Ford Under Investigation for Airbags that Cause Burn Injuries
title: Ford Under Investigation for Airbags that Cause Burn Injuries
raw_summary: Ford is currently under investigation by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation for more than a million vehicles whose front airbags could cause serious burns. According to the Preliminary Evaluation documents filed with the ODI, the investigation covers an estimated 1,236,155 Ford Explorer SUVs built between the 2021 and 2026 model years. The investigation documents explain that the ODI has received eight Vehicle Owner Questionnaires and four Early Warning Reporting “Death and Injury” reports that include allegations of burn injuries caused by the deployment of the seat-mounted side airbags. In each case, the injuries were limited to the driver, the front passenger, or both; the report didn’t detail any injuries to rear passengers or fatalities of any kind.

title: Nissan Brings The Patrol Name Back To The U.S. After Nearly 60 Years ... Kind Of
raw_summary: In a move that's either pure nostalgia-bait or an appeal to hardcore off-road nerds, Nissan is bringing the Patrol nameplate back to the U.S. for the first time since 1969. No, Nissan's Armada isn't getting a name change. Don't freak out, Armada faithful. Instead, as a celebration for the Patrol's 75th anniversary, Nissan is bringing the name back as a trim level on its full-size SUV brute. Called the Armada Patrol Pro-4X, the body-on-frame SUV adds all sorts of neat off-road extras while also not being terribly different from the normal Pro-4X it replaces, save for new Patrol badging on the tailgate, center console, door sills and floor mats. That's what it's all about, baby. There are also a handful of optional extras, like some very tough-looking Nismo-branded rock sliders and a roof rack with an incorporated light bar, that are new for 2027. They can be had along with Nismo's existing 18-inch Axis wheels, which are wrapped in BF Goodrich All-Terrain T/A K03 rubber.

Under the hood, you'll find the same twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 as the cool normal Armada , pumping out 425 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque. It's paired to a nine-speed automatic transmission that sends power to all four wheels courtesy of a full-time 4WD system and a locking rear differential. To help keep you out of trouble when you're off-road, the Patrol Pro-4X comes with height-adjustable air suspension, underbody armor, and tow hooks.

If you're the type of person who is a real nasty Nissan nerd, or you just love off-roading, perhaps the 2027 Armada Patrol Pro-4X is for you. If that's the case, you've just got to be ready to fork over $81,265, including $2,275 destination. That's no small chunk of change, but it actually undercuts this car's closest rival, the Toyota Sequoia TRD Pro , by $6,855.

I won't lie to ya, I don't completely understand the decision here for Nissan. I mean, Patrol is hardly an established nameplate in the U.S. It only existed here from 1962 to 1969, and it's been gone for a hell of a long time, so I can't imagine there's a ton of nostalgia behind it. I suppose you could point to an appeal to off-roading nerds as a reason for the name addition or perhaps Nissan is getting ready to switch the Armada's name over to Patrol in the U.S., though I sort of doubt that.

Patrol has been a part of Nissan since 1951, so there's obviously a lot of brand heritage behind it. I'm just not sure there's a lot of brand heritage behind it in the U.S. Better late than never, though, and Patrol Pro-4X does sound a bit cooler than just Pro-4X, so who am I to complain?

article_paragraphs: Chinese automaker BYD is stepping into the ultra-luxury space with its Yangwang brand, and its latest car, the Altior, features coach doors, reclining rear seats, an incredibly smooth ride, and even umbrellas that pop out of the door panels. Sound familiar? Yeah, it looks like BYD is gunning for the Rolls-Royce Phantom’s spot as the ultimate luxury sedan.

Though closer in size to the Rolls-Royce Ghost , the Altior, which means “higher” in Latin, aims to offer an elevated passenger experience rooted in Chinese tradition. Wolfgang Egger, BYD’s design director, says the Altior was inspired by the “ding,” ancient bronze cauldrons that symbolize strength, dignity, and harmony. Even the air vents have cultural significance, featuring inlays of yellow Hetian jade, which is traditionally associated with wealth, prosperity, and authority. Still, there’s more than a hint of Phantom to the exterior styling.

Jade air vents are just the tip of the Altior-sized iceberg, though. In total, the interior features 48 decorative jewelry-inspired controls. Occupants will be swaddled in full-grain leather, complemented by an ancient embroidery style that splits silk threads to create cloud-like motifs. Wool floor mats and natural wood trim round out the interior materials. Outside, the ornate grille is crafted to highlight reflecting light, and the sides of the car feature a contrasting black roof, silver accents, and sleek 21-inch wheels.

Rear zero-gravity massaging seats recline for a truly knock-out ride, especially when paired with the Altior’s relaxation mode that lowers the sun blinds, lifts the leg rests, and softens the cabin’s ambient lighting. Pair that with a 39-speaker Dynaudio sound system and a 21.4-inch overhead screen for perhaps the most exciting way to join a conference call ever invented. There are also two refrigerators—one in the front and one in the rear that can also keep things warm.

A quad-motor electric architecture powers the Altior, with each motor powering a wheel independently. An active body control system can adjust the car’s suspension in real time depending on road conditions to offer a smooth ride no matter where it’s going. BYD claims the Altior will have a range of about 621 miles on a single charge and promises speedy recharging times. Specific information about charging rates and power output hasn’t been released yet.

Yangwang seems pretty confident in the Altior’s safety system, calling it “God’s Eye.” The software includes navigation assistance on highway routes, urban streets, and from one parking spot to another. It’ll also apparently be able to float if it hits water and do a tank turn, though both of those seem to only be useful in situations that a luxury sedan likely will never find itself in.

These luxury beasts won’t reach U.S. roads, but they’re currently available for pre-order in China and are slated to start at the equivalent of around $311,540. BYD plans to bring the Altior to parts of Europe in the future.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."
